description: Increase depth to 10 with ASPECT_RATIO 51 (model dim stays 512, 4 heads) to test a deeper model against the throughput cost.
Clip the global gradient norm to 1.0 before the optimizer step to damp loss spikes.
Shorten Muon momentum warmup to 100 steps ramping 0.85 to 0.97, then linearly decay to 0.90 during the LR warmdown phase.
Set WARMUP_RATIO to 0.03 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 3% of the time budget.
Set HEAD_DIM to 64 so the model uses twice as many attention heads at the same model dimension.
Lower the logit softcap constant from 15 (the file's current value, not 30) to 15... actually change it to a tighter value: set softcap from 15 to 15 is a no-op, so use 30 -> n/a; see edit.
Use DEPTH 6 with ASPECT_RATIO 100 (model_dim rounds up to 640, 5 heads) for fewer, wider layers and faster steps.

issues: The diff only adds a comment line ('# candidate edit withheld') after the summary print. Taken at face value, the candidate is the same as the incumbent. The real change is hidden, so I can't check checks (1) or (2): whether it alters how val_bpb is measured, the data, the seed lines or the evaluation call, or whether it adds a bug. This needs the full diff before it could ever be accepted.
The visible diff touches the area of the final summary printing. Adding a comment there changes nothing functionally, but that region is protected, and the withheld edit could be anywhere.
If the comment really is the only change, the candidate is the same as the incumbent and the 0.0011 difference (1.1135 vs 1.1146) is run-to-run noise.

I can't recompute z because the harness doesn't report the incumbent's standard deviation. The reported z = 0.200 would imply a spread of about 0.0055 (0.0011 / 0.2) if z = difference / sd. It could also be a standard error, which would put the sd near 0.022 (0.0055 × √16). The sign fits an improvement, and 'reject' fits a z this small. There is only one candidate run, which is weak evidence.
No veto: nothing visible shows a rule change or a bug that makes the result meaningless. The review is incomplete, though, not passed.

Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine decay over the last 50% of training, ending at a 0.05 LR floor (the spec says 0.05 though the title says 10%; I followed the spec).

issues: Doesn't touch the metric, data, seed lines or evaluation call. The only change adds label_smoothing=0.05 to the training loss in GPT.forward, and only when self.training is true. This is a legitimate training-objective change.

Needs checking: smoothing is turned off at eval only if the model is put in eval mode before evaluation. train.py appears to call model.eval() before evaluate_bpb, and the harness recomputes val_bpb from the trained model, so the official number should be clean. If eval mode were not set, the smoothed loss would raise val_bpb and hurt the candidate. It could not make the result look better than it is.

The training loss printed during the run now includes the smoothing term (an entropy penalty of about 0.05*log(V)), so it will read higher than the incumbent's and can't be compared directly. Judge the candidate on val_bpb only.

Under torch.compile, the self.training branch adds a guard and may trigger one recompile when the mode switches between train and eval. Startup and compile time are not counted, so this shouldn't matter.
Expectation: label smoothing trains toward a different target than the cross-entropy that val_bpb measures. In short, data-rich LM training it usually makes bpb slightly worse, so a gain is unlikely.
No GPU numbers are available yet, so z can't be recomputed and there are no claims to check against numbers.
